# No Hands: The Wispr Challenge

If you can speak it, you can build it. Open to everyone

WeMakeDevs and Wispr Flow are challenging professionals to fix a real problem in their own work by building a tool for it.

The twist is that you have to use voice for the building process.

Register Get 1 month of Flow Pro free

About Wispr Flow How it works Tracks Submission Prizes FAQ

01 / About the challenge

## Build it, write it, ship it. Just don't type it.

Two weeks, from WeMakeDevs and Wispr Flow. Build a tool that fixes a problem in your own work, and use your voice to do it.

-
The problem

### Start with whatever slows you down

The report you rebuild from the same spreadsheets every Monday. The WhatsApp questions you answer with the same three replies. The CRM nobody updates, because the write-up takes longer than the call.

-
The build

### Make a tool that fixes it

Tell your AI tools what you want the way you'd tell a colleague. Wispr Flow turns it into clean text in the apps you already use, four times faster than you type.

-
The people

### You don't need to be a developer

Builders is for people who write code. No-Code is for everyone else: marketing, product, sales, ops, HR, design and more.

02 / What Wispr Flow does

## Speak naturally. Get clear, polished writing.

Hold a key and talk. What lands where your cursor is reads like you wrote it carefully, in whatever app you're in.

03 / How it works

## Register today, submit by 31 October

The challenge runs from 16 to 31 October. Build at your own pace and check in once a week.

- 01

### Step 1: Register

Set up Wispr Flow and make your first Flow the start of your project: say the problem in your work you want to fix and what your tool should do. The month of Flow Pro is on us.

- 02

### Step 2: Build with Flow

Pick a track and talk your way through it: the spec to your AI tools, the docs, the messages. Keyboard for shortcuts, voice for the rest.

- 03

### Step 3: Share every week

Upload your Wispr usage card and post your progress.

- 04

### Step 4: Submit your project

Submit it on this website by 31 October, 11:59 pm IST.

04 / Tracks

## Two tracks, one rule: use your voice

Pick one: Builders if you write code, No-Code if you don't. Either way you ship a working tool, built by voice, and one real result it produced.

01
Track 1 for developers

### Builders

A working software product that solves a problem in your own work. Dictate requirements and follow-ups into your coding tools, and let them do the coding.

- Full-stack developers

- AI engineers

- Mobile developers

- DevOps engineers

02
Track 2 for every other role

### No-Code

A working tool for your own job, made with an AI app builder or assistant, no coding needed. The judges have to be able to open and use it: an app, a shared assistant or a workflow, not a chat thread.

- Marketers

- Product managers

- Sales

- Founders

- Designers

- Human Resources

Bonus Most Wispr usage

Upload your Wispr usage card each week. Ranked by words dictated during the challenge, in any app.

Bonus Social, build in public

Post your progress with #NoHandsChallenge, tag WeMakeDevs and Wispr Flow, and add the link to your weekly check-in.

See an example project for every role

05 / Submission

## What you submit

- 01 1. A link to your working project.

- 02 2. A demo video of up to two minutes.

- 03 3. Your Wispr usage card, as a screenshot from Insights in the desktop app.

- 04 4. A few lines on the problem, who it is for and how you used Wispr.

Submissions close on Saturday 31 October at 11:59 pm IST. This is a solo challenge, so every entry is one person's project.

Sample submission Call to Follow-up Track 2: No-Code, Sales +

01 Project link

callfollowup.lovable.app

Opens without signing in. Sample call notes sit on the first screen, so a judge can try it in a minute.

02 Demo video

1:52, unlisted on YouTube

A real call ends, I hold Fn and say what happened, and the email and the CRM note appear. I dictate two fixes and send.

03 Wispr usage card

Insights screenshot, 21,480 words

Words dictated from 16 to 31 October.

04 About the project

Problem, user, and how Wispr was used

I sell to clinics, and after every call I lose half an hour writing the follow-up and updating the CRM. This is for reps on back-to-back calls. I built it in Lovable by talking through each screen with Wispr Flow, then tested it on my notes from 14 real calls. It now drafts both in under a minute.

06 / Prizes

## Prizes

Three winners take ₹1,00,000 each: the best Builders project, the best No-Code project, and whoever dictates the most with Wispr.

07 / FAQ

## Got questions?

What is No Hands?

A two-week online hackathon from WeMakeDevs and Wispr Flow, from 16 to 31 October. Build a tool that solves a problem in your own work, and use Wispr Flow to speak your prompts, instructions and docs as you build.Get 1 month of Wispr Flow Pro free

Who can take part?

Anyone in India. Professionals across all domains are welcome: founders, developers, marketing, product, HR and others. Students are welcome as well. It's a solo challenge, so no teams: you register, set up Wispr and build on your own.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. The No-Code track is built for people who don't write code, whatever your role: marketing, sales, HR, ops, design or anything else. You build your tool with an AI app builder like Lovable or an assistant like ChatGPT or Claude, and tell it what to do by talking through Wispr Flow.

What counts as a No-Code entry?

A tool someone else can open and use. An app made with an AI app builder like Lovable counts, and so does a reusable assistant, such as a custom GPT or a Gemini Gem shared by link, or a workflow in Zapier, Make or Notion that runs when the judges trigger it, from a form for example. A chat thread or a one-off prompt doesn't count. Judges need to try it without paying or asking you for access: share a public link, and if it needs a sign-in, put a test login and sample input in your description.

Does it cost anything?

No. The challenge is free to enter, and your Wispr Flow link includes 1 month of Wispr Flow Pro free.

What do I need?

A Mac or Windows computer with a microphone, and a Wispr Flow account.

Why do I set up Wispr before I register?

Because the challenge is about solving problems in a voice-first way. Your prompts, specs and docs are spoken, not typed, so Flow has to be working before you start building.

Do I have to use only my voice?

Use your voice for as much as you can: prompts, docs, messages and commit notes. You can still use the keyboard for shortcuts and small fixes. Judges look at how much of your writing went through Flow.

Can I use other tools?

Yes. Use any editor, AI assistant or app builder you like. Wispr Flow is how you talk to them.

Does the free month cover the other tools?

No. The free month is Wispr Flow Pro only. Lovable, Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude and the rest need your own accounts. Their free plans are enough for the examples on this page, but they cap how many messages or credits you get a day, so start early. You don't have to pay for anything to take part.

Can I enter more than one track?

No. Pick one track, Builders or No-Code, and submit one project in it.

How is Wispr usage measured?

From the usage card in your Wispr Flow desktop app, under Insights and Your usage. Winners' numbers are confirmed with Wispr before prizes are sent.

What if I disagree with my score?

Every score and comment is public. You can raise a question until the end of Thursday 5 November and you will get a written reply before winners are confirmed.

When are prizes sent?

Prize money is sent on Friday 6 November, the day winners are announced.

Who owns what I build?

You do. WeMakeDevs and Wispr have the right to feature your project and demo video on their channels.

Can I join after 16 October?

Yes. Registration stays open until submissions close on Saturday 31 October.

Judging

## How projects are judged

Four questions, weighted, and fixed before the challenge starts.

0 %

Does it solve a real problem in your work?

A specific problem, a clear user, and a tool that person would keep using.

0 %

Was Wispr used meaningfully?

Flow is part of the build and the workflow, and your demo and usage card show it.

0 %

Does it work?

A live link the judges can open and use.

0 %

Is the demo clear?

A two-minute video anyone can follow.

The Most Wispr usage and Social prizes are ranked on their own. Wispr usage goes by words dictated during the challenge, and Social by how clearly a post shows a real workflow.

How we keep it fair

- 01 The criteria and weights above are fixed before the challenge starts.

- 02 Every project is scored by multiple judges, and your final score is the average.

- 03 Every judge's score for every project is public on the leaderboard.

- 04 Every project gets written comments from the judges on how it could improve.

- 05 Judges do not score a project they have a connection to.

- 06 Scores are published on Wednesday 4 November, before winners are confirmed. If you think something was missed, you can raise it until the end of Thursday 5 November and you will get a written reply.

- 07 Winners' Wispr accounts are verified with Wispr before prizes are sent.

Follow it live

The leaderboard is live. It has three views: Projects, with every judge's score and comments, Wispr usage, with words dictated during the challenge, and Social, with everyone's posts.

Open the leaderboard

Judges

## The people scoring your build

The team from Wispr Flow and WeMakeDevs, scoring every submission against the same criteria.
